_comment: Single source of truth for every colour, radius and font stack the
extension paints with. It used to be declared in three places that
disagreed: popup.css's four :root blocks, options.css inheriting those,
and a whole second copy inside CARD_CSS in content/reputation-card.ts.
The card is injected into arbitrary pages behind `:host { all: initial }`
so it genuinely cannot share a stylesheet, but it can share these values:
lib/tokens.ts builds its CSS text from this file, and
scripts/gen-tokens.mjs writes src/tokens.css from the same file (run from
scripts/build.mjs, so a drifted checkout cannot ship).
Values mirror app/globals.css in the main repo, INCLUDING the three token
splits that file's own comments justify. Read those before editing a
colour here; the short version:
primary / primaryText  The brand blue is a BUTTON FILL, paired with a
near-black primaryFg at 7:1. Painted as TEXT on a light surface the
same value measures 2.0:1, so text, focus rings and selected-state
edges take primaryText instead: same hue and saturation, lightness
lowered to clear AA (4.56:1 on bg, 5.15:1 on card). In dark mode the
brand blue already measures 7.6:1 as text, so the two are identical
there and nothing changes.
border / input  border is a CONTAINER edge (a card, a panel, a divider)
and SC 1.4.11 does not reach it: it is 1.36:1 on bg and that is
correct for the job. input is a CONTROL edge, the thing that tells you
a text field, a switch or an outline button is there. That IS 1.4.11,
so it carries a real 3:1 floor against every resting surface a control
is placed on.
severity / severityText  The severity chip paints the tint, the border
and the dot from severity, and the LABEL from severityText. globals.css
predicted exactly this and named the fix: 'the pale TINT behind a badge
comes from the true amber while the text on it comes from this
darkened value'. The extension needs it because the label sits on a
tint OF ITS OWN HUE, which lifts the surface and costs contrast the
app's own numbers were never measured against.
severity is BYTE-IDENTICAL to --severity-* in app/globals.css and must
stay that way: tests/extension/pure-modules.test.ts parses that file
and compares channel by channel. Read the long comment above the
--severity-* block there before touching these. The short version is
that the ramp is an ORDERED scale and its steps have to be visible in
lightness, not only in hue, or critical/high/medium collapse into one
colour in greyscale and to a red-green colour vision deficiency. That
ordering lives in these five values, so severityText is derived from
them and only where a chip's own tint forces it: light medium and low,
dark critical and info. The other six are identical to their fill.
success / warning / danger / info need no split: darkening the value
darkens its own tint with it, and a lower lightness clears AA on both.
WHY THIS IS A COPY AND NOT DERIVED FROM app/globals.css AT BUILD TIME:
extension/ builds from its own directory alone. scripts/package-source.mjs
zips exactly that directory as the source archive AMO reviewers build from,
so a generator reaching up into ../app would produce an archive that cannot
be built. The enforcement lives in the cross-check test instead, which is
what caught the last drift. Anything above that is NOT marked
byte-identical is the extension's own and deliberately diverges.
Every ratio quoted above and in extension/tests/contrast.test.ts is
computed, not estimated. Run that suite after changing anything here.

metrics.font: system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
metrics.mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace
